1.0.s.en: (1) The numbering of the people and the appointment of heads from the tribes

1.0.0.en: After the people came out of the land of bondage (the Book of Exodus), the building of the tabernacle of meeting (the house of God) was among the most important matters and the first of them; that is, God had to set apart a house before the journey began. After the tabernacle was built (Ex 40:17), the Lord spoke to Moses from it, first concerning the laws, the sacrifices and the feasts (Lev 1:1). The second discourse came here, and its time was fixed as the second month of the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt. Since the Book of Exodus had mentioned that the arrival in the wilderness was in the third month of the first year, this discourse with Moses took place eleven months after they reached the wilderness.

1.0.1.en: After the tabernacle of meeting was built, God always spoke from it, as though He wished to say to everyone who wants to know the voice of God and His will in his life: Come to My Church, for there I will hear you and speak with you as well. This is why we call the Church "the house of God." So if you are seeking God, beloved, do not waste your time; go to His house, speak with Him and listen to Him, and He will speak with you.

1.1.1.en: The house of their fathers: that is, the households.

1.1.2.en: By their armies: the divisions to which they belong according to the houses, the families and the tribes. The subject of the Lord's words to Moses was the command to number the people, "all the congregation," that is, to count the males able to go to war, whom God defined as those above twenty years of age. The Lord charged Moses and his brother Aaron to supervise the numbering themselves and under their direct responsibility, because of the importance of the matter.

1.1.3.en: This numbering is the first numbering of the children of Israel who came out of Egypt. There is another opinion, which is that Moses had made another numbering before the tabernacle of meeting was set up, and collected from the males the silver that went into the building of the tabernacle (Ex 38:25, 26).

1.2.0.en: Because of the difficulty and importance of the work, God commanded Moses and Aaron to take the help of twelve men, who were the heads of the tribes, "each one head of the house of his fathers," to complete this counting. Here God teaches us two important things: the first is organization and prior planning for any work we undertake, and the other is an important principle, namely seeking the help of others and employing their abilities so that the work is accomplished more quickly and with the least weariness, as it also shows the role of the laity in the service of the Church.

1.3.0.en: God mentioned to Moses and Aaron the names of the heads of the tribes and specified them, and the writing of their names here means that God is the One who chooses and calls, for He knows who is fit for this task. The mention of their names is also an honor and a lasting memorial to them and to their labors, for God does not forget anyone's labor. The indication here is also clear to us that whoever labors for the sake of Christ, His Church and His people will have his name written in the Book of Life in the Kingdom of Heaven. It is noticed that God mentioned first the name of the tribe and then the one responsible for numbering it, for we always belong to our spiritual fathers, as an extension of them and the fruit of their labor in us.

1.3.1.en: Elizur: its meaning is God is a rock, and he is head of the tribe of Reuben.

1.3.2.en: Shelumiel (v. 6): peace of God, and he is head of the tribe of Simeon.

1.3.3.en: Nahshon (v. 7): its meaning is serpent; he was the brother of Aaron's wife, is head of the tribe of Judah, and is mentioned in the genealogy of Christ (Mt 1:4). Nethaneel (v. 8): its meaning is God has given, and he is head of the tribe of Issachar.

1.3.4.en: Eliab (v. 9): God is Father, and he is head of the tribe of Zebulun.

1.3.5.en: The children of Joseph (v. 10): it is noticed that Joseph did not have a tribe of his own, although he was of the loins of Jacob, the father of all the tribes; but because God blessed Joseph with a blessing greater than all his brothers, he came to have two tribes in the persons of his sons (Manasseh and Ephraim). Elishama: God is my salvation, and he is head of the tribe of Ephraim.

1.3.6.en: Gamaliel: God repays the kindness (the reward), and he is head of the tribe of Manasseh.

1.3.7.en: Abidan (v. 11): my father is judge, and he is head of the tribe of Benjamin.

1.3.8.en: Ahiezer (v. 12): my brother is for help, and he is head of the tribe of Dan.

1.3.9.en: Pagiel (v. 13): God meets, and he is head of the tribe of Asher.

1.3.10.en: Eliasaph (v. 14): God has added to me, and he is head of the tribe of Gad.

1.3.11.en: Ahira (v. 15): its meaning is my brother is evil, and he is head of the tribe of Naphtali.

1.4.0.en: After the choosing of the men, Moses the prophet declares to us their standing and the greatness of their rank among the people, making clear that they were in fact the most worthy of all to be chosen, for they were known to the whole people and were indeed the heads of the tribes and the source of their confidence, and they were also their judges, "heads of thousands"; for Moses had chosen for his people rulers of tens, rulers of fifties, rulers of hundreds and rulers of thousands to help him in governing and judging the people's troubles, in keeping with the counsel of his father-in-law Jethro, after he had been judging alone and it had wearied him greatly (Ex 18:21-23).

1.5.s.en: (2) The actual numbering and the number of males in each tribe

1.5.0.en: The work began at once, as the Lord had said, for God's word to Moses had come on the first of the second month (v. 1), and here too the same time is mentioned for the beginning of the work. The work began with the whole congregation of the people gathering, divided by tribes; and since this numbering was only of the males able to go to war, these chosen heads recorded their names as the first of those numbered, so "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."

1.5.1.en: By their polls: that is, this counting was exact and left out none of the males above twenty years of age.

1.5.2.en: Let us learn two things from this: the first is quickness in responding to God's word and His commandments and not postponing spiritual work, for quickness of response shows and brings out our love and obedience toward God; and the second is exactness and diligence in carrying out this work, for speed must not come at the expense of exactness, otherwise it would have no value.

1.6.0.en: Their generations: that is, their births.

1.6.1.en: From twenty years old: that is, whoever was twenty years old, with no upper age limit so long as he was able to go to war.

1.6.2.en: The numbering began with the tribe of Reuben, who was indeed Jacob's firstborn in the flesh, even though the spiritual blessing went to Joseph because Reuben had angered his father (Gen 49:3, 4). The numbering of each tribe was recorded separately first. It is noticed in the numbering of each tribe:

1.6.3.en: (1) That it was approximate to the nearest hundred, so the numbers of tens or units were not mentioned in this numbering. (2) The emphasis on exactness, for the twelve heads of the tribes took part in it together with both "Moses" and "Aaron."

1.6.4.en: (3) The census states that the total number of all the males of the tribes reached 603,550 (v. 46), because if the units and tens were actually added up, this figure was rounded to the nearest ten. Statisticians in modern times say, according to population rates, that this means the number of the whole people was about two and a half million.

1.6.5.en: (4) The expression "all that were able to go forth to war" (v. 45) is an expression we ought to contemplate spiritually, for the spiritual life is a life of striving for the Lord and a war against Satan and the lusts of the world, and we have all come out of Baptism as spiritual soldiers counted in the army of God (2 Tim 2:3), and this war of ours continues throughout the days of our sojourn on earth. So do not be careless, my beloved brother, but trust in God's help to you, for God wants for you the victory and the crown, but you must want them too.

1.6.6.en: (5) This numbering also shows God's blessing upon the people, as His earlier promise to their great father Abraham (Gen 12:2), since their number when they entered Egypt with Jacob was 75 souls, and now, after their coming out of Egypt, their number had reached two and a half million.

1.6.7.en: (6) The Book of Exodus (Ex 12:37) mentions that the number of men who came out of Egypt after the ten plagues was six hundred thousand, while this census states that their number was six hundred thousand, three thousand, five hundred and fifty; the difference between the two numbers is the number of males who reached the age of twenty in the period of thirteen months from their coming out of Egypt to the beginning of the second month of the second year. (7) The census was useful in knowing the genealogies of the children of Israel, the importance of which appeared in knowing the genealogy of Christ.

1.7.s.en: (3) The Levites were not numbered, and their duties

1.7.0.en: These verses show that, on the basis of God's command to Moses and His speaking with him (v. 1), the males of the tribe of Levi, that is, the Levites, were not counted or numbered, and their numbers were not included in the total of those going out to war, since God had prepared for them another work no less important than war itself, namely the service of the tabernacle of meeting.

1.8.0.en: The tabernacle of the testimony: the tabernacle of meeting, which took this name because it contained within it the two tablets of the covenant, or the testimony, that is, the Ten Commandments.

1.8.1.en: Round about the tabernacle shall they encamp: the Levites used to dwell around the tabernacle of meeting on the north, west and south sides, while the priests dwelt on the east side before the door of the tabernacle (ch. 2). Here the task of the Levites becomes clear: it is to care for and guard the tabernacle of meeting and everything connected with it and all its inner contents, "the vessels thereof"; they alone are assigned to carry the tabernacle when traveling and journeying, and they perform the service inside it and outside it and dwell around it.

1.9.0.en: They alone also have the right to take its parts apart when journeying and to set it up in the midst of the people when they settle. And everyone who is not of the tribe of Levi, that is, a stranger, is put to death, according to God's command, if he draws near, or touches, or lays a hand on the components or any part of the tabernacle.

1.10.0.en: His camp: the place of his dwelling.

1.10.1.en: His standard: a flag or banner belonging to each tribe.

1.10.2.en: By their armies: that is, the tribe with its males counted for war.

1.10.3.en: When they settle and the tabernacle of meeting is set up, the people gather in order around the tabernacle, each tribe having its place and its flag, "its standard," and this will be discussed in detail in the second chapter.

1.11.0.en: As for the tents of the Levites, they are to be the closest to the tabernacle of meeting and around it, and this is a second confirmation of what God had already mentioned in (v. 51), and it shows that their nearness to the tabernacle is because of their service to His house and their keeping the rites and ordinances of worship. And God charges all His people to carry out His word in this matter, or else the whole people would be exposed to wrath and punishment.

1.12.0.en: The conclusion of this chapter comes to show that what the Lord commanded "Moses" in (v. 1) was carried out with the utmost exactness, fear and respect.

1.12.1.en: My beloved brother, have you seen with me how great was God's care for His house, that is, the tabernacle of meeting, and how He set apart for it a whole tribe, and how He kept strangers from drawing near it?! My brother, the tabernacle was a type of the Church of the New Testament, and with all it contained it did not reach the glory of the Church of God, which offers His Body and Blood. Do we then respect the house of God and revere it as is fitting? Be careful, beloved, and keep the words of the Lord Christ always in your ear, "The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up" (Jn 2:17), as you deal with His Church and its sacraments.

1.12.2.en: The tribes and their encampment around the tabernacle: introduction:

1.12.3.en: This chapter shows us that our God is a God of order and arrangement, and how He divided the twelve tribes into four groups, each group pitching its tents on one of the four sides of the tabernacle of meeting, and likewise God set an order for the journeying of the congregation when they travel.

2.0.s.en: (1) The order and place of encampment of the tribes

2.0.0.en: His standard: a piece of cloth bearing some symbol or drawing or color.

2.0.1.en: Over against: in front of, or opposite.

2.0.2.en: The discourse was from God, the Supreme Commander of the march of His people, directed to the earthly leaders, that is, Moses and Aaron, and the subject of the discourse was how the tribes were to dwell around the tabernacle when it was set up .. and God's first command was that each group should have a flag that distinguishes it; and because each group consists of three tribes, the interpreters also saw that each tribe had another, smaller flag that distinguished it within the group. The flag of each tribe was distinct from the flags of the other tribes, and perhaps it bore what represents the prophecies of Jacob to his sons (Gen 49). The expression "round about it they shall encamp" is a beautiful expression showing God's concern that His people be around Him, while He is their God dwelling in their midst, caring for their every need.

2.0.3.en: We too have come to have a standard and a sign in the drawing of the holy Cross, by which we remember and call to mind the sufferings of our Redeemer the Lord Jesus and His love for us. Take care, my brother, to befriend this sign in all your works, for its power is exceedingly wonderful.

2.1.0.en: Camp: the place where the tents are pitched.

2.1.1.en: Camp of Dan, comprising the tribes of Dan, Asher and Naphtali. Merarites. Camp of Ephraim, comprising the tribes of north Ephraim, Manasseh and Benjamin. The outer court. Altar of burnt offering. Gershonites. The laver. East. West. Tabernacle of meeting. Moses and Aaron and his sons. Judah, Issachar and Zebulun. South. Camp of Judah, comprising the tribes. Kohathites. Camp of Reuben, comprising the tribes of Reuben, Simeon, Figure (1) The place of encampment of the tribes around the tabernacle. God began by fixing the place of the tents of the first group, which consists of three tribes, namely Judah, Issachar and Zebulun (Figure 1), and the following is noticed in this group:

2.1.2.en: 1- Although they are three tribes, they were called "the camp of Judah," because he is the eldest and foremost among his brothers, and from him Christ will come.

2.1.3.en: 2- This group occupied the eastern place, that is, in front of the main and only door of the tabernacle of meeting. And before it, on the side of the door, dwell Moses and Aaron and the rest of the priests. The camp of Judah was two thousand cubits from the tabernacle, that is, about one kilometer, and the farthest of its tents were about 1.5 km away, so that all the people were able to reach the tabernacle of meeting easily.

2.1.4.en: 3- The names of the heads of the tribes are mentioned to show their standing and their authority in the organization; they are the same heads who helped Moses and Aaron in the counting and numbering of the people (ch. 1).

2.1.5.en: 4- The number of males previously counted and ready for war is also mentioned, and after the number of the males of each tribe was given, they were all added together as the total of one group, namely "the camp of Judah," so the number of males of the eastern group reached one hundred and eighty-six thousand four hundred.

2.1.6.en: They shall first set forth: that is, they are the first people to take down their tents and lead the people on the march. It is noticed that in the tenth chapter too he will explain more fully the manner of the people's journeying and the order of the tribes in it.

2.2.0.en: The south: that is, the southern side.

2.2.1.en: God assigned the southern side for the encampment of three other tribes, namely the tribes of Reuben, Simeon and Gad, but the camp or group took the name of Reuben as the tribe placed at the head of the group, as happened with the group of Judah. Here too the males of each tribe were counted separately, and then the total of the whole group came to one hundred and fifty-one thousand four hundred and fifty, that is, the males numbered for war.

2.2.2.en: They shall set forth second: that is, when journeying they are the second group after the group of Judah.

2.3.s.en: (2) The order of the journeying of the Levites and the rest of the tribes

2.3.0.en: After the groups of Judah and Reuben set forth, who are six tribes, that is, half the people, the tabernacle too is taken down and journeys in the midst of the people, that is, two groups, then the tabernacle, and after them two groups; and because the Levites alone have the right to carry the tabernacle with all its contents and vessels, their journeying is mentioned here as accompanying the journeying of the tabernacle.

2.3.1.en: Every man in his place by their standards: the Levites did not journey all at once but in companies, each company charged with carrying certain parts, and the order of the journeying of these companies comes as the tenth chapter will explain. These companies of the Levites were the "Gershonites," the "Merarites" and the "Kohathites," and each company among them had a flag or standard that distinguished it, and each of the three companies dwelt on a different side of the tabernacle, as the drawing at the end of the chapter shows.

2.4.0.en: As for the third group, it bore the name of Ephraim the son of Joseph and included, as usual, three tribes: with him were the tribe of Manasseh, the brother of Ephraim, and Benjamin. The names of the heads of the tribes and the number of those mustered for war for each tribe separately were also mentioned, and then the total of the three tribes together, and the total reached one hundred and eight thousand one hundred. Their order of journeying among the tribes was also the third.

2.5.0.en: Finally comes the fourth group, which was named "Dan" and also included the tribes of Asher and Naphtali, and the total of those reckoned in it for war was one hundred and fifty-seven thousand six hundred, and this fourth group was the last group in the journeying.

2.5.1.en: The following is noticed in the order of the encampment of the tribes:

2.5.2.en: 1- God's concern for order and arrangement, so that this might be the way of His people in their lives and dealings.

2.5.3.en: 2- Each of the four groups encamped around the tabernacle of meeting was of one kin: the group of Judah, encamped east of the tabernacle, included three of the sons of Leah, namely Judah, Issachar and Zebulun; the group of Reuben, encamped south of the tabernacle, included two of the sons of Leah, namely Reuben and Simeon, while Gad is the son of Zilpah, Leah's maid. The third group, encamped west of the tabernacle, is the group of Ephraim, which included Ephraim and Manasseh, the sons of Joseph, and Benjamin his brother, all of them of the offspring of Rachel. As for the fourth group, which encamps north of the tabernacle, it is the group of Dan and includes Dan and Naphtali, the sons of Bilhah, and Asher the son of Zilpah.

2.5.4.en: 3- The tribe of Levi encamps around the tabernacle and close to it on three sides because they are charged with the service of the house of the Lord, while the priests encamp on the east side before the door of the tabernacle to perform their work in it.

2.5.5.en: 4- It is noticed that the number of soldiers in the first group, which is the group of Judah that goes before the people when they set forth, includes the greatest number of soldiers, followed in number of soldiers by the fourth group, the group of Dan, which is in the rear, while the second and third groups are fewer in number and are in the middle, in order to protect the people, so that its front and its rear are strong to face the enemies.

2.5.6.en: 5- The tabernacle of meeting is in the midst of the tribes of Israel, whether encamping or journeying, in order to guard it.

2.6.0.en: As a conclusion to what came in this chapter, the grand and final total of the whole number is mentioned, as it also came at the end of the first chapter (v. 46), including all the tribes or the four groups.

2.7.0.en: Moses the prophet makes clear here the Lord's command to him not to number the Levites with the people, since they had another service and became the portion of the Lord and servants of His house, although the third chapter will show us that there was also a numbering of the Levites that was their own, but we shall learn of it in its time.

2.8.0.en: And so the people kept the established order throughout nearly forty years, in their journeying and encamping, and they always carried their standards belonging to each group, each tribe and each family. We can draw some beneficial spiritual meanings from what came in this chapter:

2.8.1.en: 1- God shows His love for us, for He wants to dwell in our midst as a tender Father, and for His children to gather around Him.

2.8.2.en: 2- In His care for us, God set an order for His people in journeying and encamping, for order saves time and prevents confusion and children's getting lost among the great people.

2.8.3.en: 3- The high standards were to guide anyone who strayed from his people during the journey: there was a standard for the group, another for the tribe and a smaller one for the family ... and this reminds us of the high lighthouse of the Church, guiding everyone who has strayed and wandered in the exile of the world.

2.8.4.en: 4- We too must keep the commandments of the Lord during the journey of life, for it is easy for us also to wander in the world in which we live and lose our way to heaven. Let us fix our eyes on the Lord and His standard, which is His Cross, and keep our ears and hearts subject to all that He tells us, and deliverance will be written for us.

2.8.5.en: It is good that God be your leader in all your steps, so that you walk through life at peace, by lifting your prayers to Him before every work and by submitting to the guidance of the Church even if it differs from the thoughts of the world. The descendants of Moses and Aaron and the account of the Levites
